text: A parametrized curve describes position as a parameter changes. This formula traces a circle of radius two. Differentiating gives the velocity vector; its length is two, so equal changes in the parameter correspond to twice that much traveled arc length.
title: Idea 1

text: Speed depends on parameterization, while the geometric path remains the same. Using arc length s as the parameter makes speed one. The unit tangent then records direction alone, separating how the curve turns from how quickly it is traversed.
title: Idea 2

text: Curvature measures the rate at which the unit tangent changes per unit arc length. A radius-two circle has curvature one half; a larger circle turns less sharply. This is curve curvature, not the Gaussian curvature assigned to a surface.
title: Idea 3

text: A surface uses two parameters instead of one. On this paraboloid, changing u or v gives two independent tangent directions. Their span is the tangent plane. Independence of these parameter derivatives is the regularity condition preventing a collapsed coordinate patch.
title: Idea 4
